glosses: To help forward; to assist.

examples.text:
In happie houre we haue ſet the Crowne
Upon your Kingly head, that ſeeks our honor,
In ioyning with the man, ordain’d by heauen
To further euerie action to the beſt.

Upon this he brought me a cotton bag and giving it to me, said, "Take this bag and fill it with pebbles from the beach and go forth with a company of the townsfolk to whom I will give a charge respecting thee. glosses: To encourage growth; to support progress or growth of something; to promote.

examples.text: Further the economy.
to further the peace process

glosses: More distant; relatively distant.

examples.text: See those two lampposts? Run to the further one.
He was standing at the further end of the corridor.

glosses: More, additional.

examples.text: I have one further comment to make.

This time Cudicini was left helpless when Natcho stepped up to expertly curl the ball into the top corner.
That was the cue for further pressure from the Russian side and it took further Cudicini saves to keep the score down.

glosses: To, at or over a greater distance in space, time or other extent.

examples.text: I can run further than you.
I live a little further out of town.
How was your company doing ten years further back?

“A very welcome, kind, useful present, that means to the parish. By the way, Hopkins, let this go no further. We don't want the tale running round that a rich person has arrived. Churchill, my dear fellow, we have such greedy sharks, and wolves in lamb's clothing.[…]”

glosses: To a greater extent or degree.

examples.text: Of the two civilisations, this one was further advanced.
I do not propose to discuss it any further. - Please, let me explain just a little further.

glosses: Beyond what is already stated or is already the case.

examples.text: Chapter 10 further explains the ideas introduced in Chapter 9.

The use of algorithms in policing is one example of their increasing influence on our lives.[…]who, if anyone, is policing their use[?] Such concerns were sharpened further by the continuing revelations about how the US National Security Agency (NSA) has been using algorithms to help it interpret the colossal amounts of data it has collected from its covert dragnet of international telecommunications.

glosses: Also; in addition; furthermore; moreover.

examples.text: It is overlong, and further, it makes no sense.
I claim furthermore that he did not own the company but only worked there.
Further, besides sensible things and Forms he says there are the objects of mathematics, which occupy an intermediate position,[…].

glosses: Following on (from).

examples.text: Further to our recent telephone call, I am writing to clarify certain points raised.
